name: rowCollapse
title: Extracts one cell per row from a matrix

origin.description: Extracts one cell per row (column) from a matrix.
origin.usage: rowCollapse(x, idxs, rows = NULL, dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: An index vector of (maximum) length N specifying the columns to be extracted.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: idxs is recycled to the number of rows, then used to pick from 0:(ncol - 1). Those offsets become column-major positions. rows uses matrix subscripting. A positive index past the end of idxs is NA. A positive index past the end of rows is an error.
origin.value: A vector of length N, one cell from each selected row, with the storage mode of x.

translation.description: Extracts one cell per row from a matrix.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array, or a one-dimensional vector when dim is given. A two-dimensional array is read with axis 0 as rows and axis 1 as columns, matching the printed R matrix. Logical x is kept as logical. A three-dimensional array is rejected.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based columns to extract, one per row. The vector is recycled to the number of rows. None is NULL and returns an empty vector. Zero is dropped and a negative value excludes, as in R vector subscripting. A positive index past the last column is a missing value. Numeric values are truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to keep before the extraction. None uses every row. This is matrix subscripting: a positive index past the end is an error, and a logical index longer than the row count is an error.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the shape of x, also when x is not a matrix. This is dim. When x is one-dimensional, the values fill that shape in column-major order. idxs is recycled to the first of these lengths.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: This is useNames, checked with R's if. The result is a plain array; names are not attached. A missing value or a vector longer than one is an error.

translation.details: The positions are the ones built in R/rowCollapse.R. idxs is repeated to the row count, rows subsets both the matrix and that index, and each kept index selects from 0:(ncol - 1). The selected offsets are added to 1:nrow with R's recycling, including the warning when the lengths do not divide. When ncol is 0, that colon is c(0, -1). Integer x returns int32, and a missing integer is -2147483648. Double missing values are NaN.
translation.value: A one-dimensional array of length N, one cell from each selected row. Double x returns float64. Integer x returns int32. Logical x returns bool, or an object array when a missing value is required.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowcollapse import rowCollapse

rowCollapse(np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F"), [1, 2, 3])
